analysis.investment_thesis: Aurionpro has undergone a genuine business transformation — revenue surged at ~33% CAGR from FY2022–2025, driven by banking technology and nascent AI products (Arya.ai, AryaXAI) in a large, underpenetrated Indian fintech TAM. However, the long-term 9-year revenue CAGR of only 5.7% and low promoter holding of 26.88% raise questions about management conviction and the durability of this acceleration.
key_strengths: Recent growth acceleration is Fisher-worthy: revenue grew 34.6% (FY24) and 32.2% (FY25), with operating income nearly doubling in 3 years (INR 111→242 Cr).
Near debt-free balance sheet (D/E 0.02, borrowings down to INR 30 Cr) with INR 269 Cr cash — gives capital for acquisitions and R&D without dilution risk.
Diversified banking-tech product portfolio (AI, trade finance, digital banking, smart city) gives multiple growth vectors in a structurally expanding sector.
key_risks: 9-year revenue CAGR of only 5.7% (2016→2025) exposes a decade of stagnation; the current acceleration must be proved durable before Fisher-style conviction is warranted.
Promoter holding at only 26.88% is concerningly low — management lacks the 'skin in the game' Fisher considers essential for long-term-oriented stewardship.

Free cash flow of INR 62 Cr in FY25 vs. net profit of INR 188 Cr signals a wide conversion gap; heavy investing outflows (-INR 421 Cr in FY25) suggest acquisition-driven growth whose returns are unproven.
red_flags: 2021 net loss of -INR 192 Cr (fuelled by -INR 118 Cr other income write-down) reveals prior strategic missteps and asset write-offs — a cautionary signal about management's historical capital allocation.
Equity base ballooned from INR 930 Cr to INR 1,606 Cr in one year alongside positive financing CF of INR 283 Cr — likely a significant equity raise that dilutes existing shareholders.
ROE of 15.3% is below the 20%+ threshold Fisher demands; despite improving earnings, the capital base is growing faster than returns.
analysis.detailed_analysis:
From my Scuttlebutt perspective, Aurionpro is a genuinely interesting but imperfect growth story. The recent three-year trajectory is the best argument for the stock: revenues went from INR 505 Cr (FY22) to INR 1,173 Cr (FY25), operating income from INR 111 Cr to INR 242 Cr, and net profit from INR 76 Cr to INR 188 Cr — all at 30%+ CAGR. The banking-tech TAM (enterprise lending, trade finance, digital banking, AI decisioning) is large and growing, and the AI products (Arya.ai, AryaXAI) represent genuine innovation potential if they gain enterprise traction. At a forward P/E of ~17x on what appears to be a ~30% earnings grower, the valuation is not demanding.

However, my checklist raises doubts. The 9-year revenue CAGR of 5.7% tells me management spent most of the last decade treading water, and the 2021 large loss (-INR 192 Cr net) confirms a prior strategic stumble. A great growth company compounds consistently; this one clearly did not. The promoter at 26.88% lacks the committed founder-operator profile I insist upon. Heavy investing outflows of -INR 421 Cr in FY25 suggest inorganic growth dependence — acquisitions are inherently uncertain, and the FCF/profit gap (INR 62 Cr vs. INR 188 Cr) means quality of earnings needs close monitoring. I would watch two more years of sustained organic revenue growth and FCF improvement before building meaningful conviction.
